# LinkedIn cuts Spark shuffle costs 90% as Anthropic buys a confidential-computing data startup

A quiet news day across all three domains, with most feeds dominated by SEO tutorials, interview-prep content and Google News homonym noise rather than breaking stories. The clearest signal came from Data Engineering Weekly's roundup of production infrastructure write-ups and two data-platform acquisitions, alongside a sharp reminder that a green dbt test suite doesn't guarantee correct data.

## Top 5 across domains
- **[Data Engineering]** [Data Engineering Weekly #292](https://www.dataengineeringweekly.com/p/data-engineering-weekly-292) covers LinkedIn moving Spark and Flink shuffle to a remote NVMe-backed service (Apache Celeborn), cutting Spark runtimes 14% and shuffle costs 90%, plus Netflix's observability knowledge graph and Datalogy's on-demand training-data pipeline.
- **[Data Platform Engineering]** [Anthropic acquired confidential-computing startup Opaque Systems](https://news.google.?oc=5), building secure data collaboration infrastructure — a bet on confidential computing for data clean rooms.
- **[Data Engineering]** Google shipped [EmbeddingGemma 2](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/embeddinggemma-2-multimodal/?utm_campaign=infoq_content&utm_source=infoq&utm_medium=feed&utm_term=AI%2C+ML+%26+Data+Engineering), an Apache 2.0, open-weight multimodal embedding model for on-device semantic search and RAG.
- **[Analytics Engineering]** A dbt practitioner [planted bugs in a rebuilt pipeline](https://medium.com/@immairaj/i-rebuilt-my-hand-written-pipeline-in-dbt-and-planted-the-bugs-myself-dc47e145b772?source=rss------dbt-5) and found all 31 tests passed even as three rows silently vanished.
- **[Data Platform Engineering]** Canadian consultancy [Adastra acquired Poland-based Infinite Services](https://news.google.?oc=5), expanding its footprint among data and AI consultancies.
